bullets.title: FOXA acquires ROKU for $160/sh; $22B EV, mixed analyst reactions
bullets.body: Fox Corp agreed to acquire Roku for $160/share (60% cash/40% stock) at a ~$22B enterprise value. Citi's Jason Bazinet sees $400M in synergies worth 7x EV/EBITDA; pro-forma entity targets $23B revenue and $5B EBITDA by FY27E growing ~7% CAGR with $9-10 FCF/share by FY30, shifting to 50% streaming/CTV by FY30. FOXA fell ~17% on deal announcement while ROKU traded down ~2%; Wedbush downgraded ROKU to Neutral (PT $155) post-deal.

bullets.title: TTD: Fox-Roku deal seen as positive; take rate stabilizing at 20%
bullets.body: Benchmark notes FOXA's ROKU acquisition is positive for TTD as open programmatic access via Trade Desk is essential for Fox to maximize demand flows and monetization of the combined entity. DA Davidson separately notes TTD's long-term take rate likely stabilizes around 20%; Publicis controls only a small portion of current TTD clients and ChatGPT monetization discussions are ongoing but the company is quiet on the topic.

bullets.title: NVDA: Inference share rises to 74%; Blackwell leads agentic AI benchmarks; $25B debt raise planned
bullets.body: NVDA's inference chip market share rose to 74% from 66% over the past year, with inference expected to reach two-thirds of AI workloads by end-2026 (up from one-third in 2023). Blackwell NVL72 scored highest on the first agentic AI benchmark (AgentPerf), running 20x more agents/MW than HGX H200. NVDA plans to raise $25B in new debt — its first corporate bond sale since 2021.

bullets.title: WDC/STX: HDD bull case goes viral; +16%/+9% on Asia checks, EPS well above consensus
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's bullish HDD sector update citing Asia supply chain checks drove WDC +16% and STX +9% in Monday's session; analysts see HDD vendors targeting $25-30/TB pricing over 2-3 years vs. current <$15, with WDC FY28 EPS base case ~70% above consensus. Mizuho confirmed CPO and 800VDC shipment schedules remain on track for 2028-2029 volume production. Both stocks are up ~270-280% YTD before these moves.

bullets.title: META: Threads hits 500M MAUs; new AI features, 'AI Mode' search across FB posts
bullets.body: META's Threads platform reached 500M MAUs, adding 100M users in ~10 months from 400M in August 2025, with new personalization tools ('Your Algo') and Communities features launching. META is also rolling out 'AI Mode' search across Facebook public posts. The stock fell ~4% on Monday amid a broader internet group selloff, trading at ~17x '26 EPS vs. its TTM multiple of ~24x.

bullets.title: AMZN/GOOGL/META/APP: Internet mega-caps down 3-11% as AI hardware vs. software debate weighs
bullets.body: Internet names fell ~3% as a group on Monday vs. SPX/NDX up 1-2%; AMZN and META led declines at -3%/-4%, GOOGL -2%, UBER/DASH -3-4%, and APP was the largest faller at -11%. Current multiples: AMZN/GOOGL/META at 25x/24x/17x '26E EPS, down 21%/5%/30% vs. TTM levels. The selloff reflects investor debate over AI capex allocation between hardware and software beneficiaries.

bullets.title: VZ: New Simplicity Plan shifts device subsidies to subscription model; industry pricing read-across
bullets.body: Verizon announced its Simplicity Plan ($30/month base, +$35 Plus, +$50 Pro tiers), Verizon One bundle ($70/month unlimited mobile + 500 Mbps home internet), a 3% loyalty rebate program, and elimination of activation/upgrade fees ($40/device). KeyBanc (Sector Weight, $45 PT) notes the shift from upfront device subsidies to subscription-based payments is too early to assess; Citi flags substantial industry pricing strategy read-across with potential share loss to AT&T and T-Mobile if promotions moderate.

bullets.title: HOOD: 10% RIF; KeyBanc maintains $100 PT on record volume momentum
bullets.body: Robinhood announced a ~10% FTE reduction (~290 roles) and closure of open positions, framing it as accelerating product velocity. Expected restructuring charges of ~$28M in 2Q26 (~$20M severance, ~$8M SBC) with savings expected to flow through the P&L. KeyBanc maintains $100 PT (59.5x FY26 EPS), noting record volumes across equities, options, and prediction markets in June. HOOD traded +1.9% premarket despite the cuts.

bullets.title: ACN: Q3 earnings 6/18; consensus $18.78B revenue, $3.71 EPS; options imply ~7.5% move
bullets.body: Accenture reports Q3 on June 18 with consensus revenue of $18.78B (vs. guidance midpoint $18.68B) and EPS of $3.71. ACN has beaten revenue in 16 of 20 quarters and EPS in 18 of 20, but forward guidance beats in only 6 of 18. Near-term options imply ~7.5% move; ACN is up 15.3% since March 18 vs. S&P 500 +14.0%. Last four earnings moves: +4%, -1%, -3%, +7%.

bullets.title: PLTR: Wolfe upgrades to Peer Perform from Underperform; valuation limits upside at 30x CY27 revenue
bullets.body: Wolfe relaunched PLTR coverage at Peer Perform (upgraded from Underperform), acknowledging it was wrong on FDE scalability, pilot fade, and margin concerns. PLTR is described as best-in-class at driving enterprise AI adoption; sales quota attainment at record levels for three consecutive quarters. However, at ~30x CY27 revenue and ~65x EPS (~2x megacap software peers), stock needs positive estimate revisions for meaningful outperformance.

bullets.title: RBLX: Age-based accounts rolled out globally; QTD CCUs +9% y/y, on track for $1.55-1.61B 2Q26 bookings
bullets.body: Roblox rolled out age-based accounts globally on schedule; current QTD CCUs are +9% vs. 2Q25 (vs. peak CCUs down 4% y/y at 14.1M), aided by the Grow a Garden 2 release. Management reiterated 2Q26 bookings guidance of $1.55-1.61B. Citi views the CCU trajectory constructively.

bullets.title: AVGO: Custom XPU role intact but momentum rotation away after earnings; $35B Apollo/Blackstone vehicle
bullets.body: AVGO is the key custom silicon (XPU) player for GOOGL, META, MSFT, and OpenAI, deploying a $35B financing vehicle with Apollo and Blackstone. However, AVGO fell 22% post-earnings as momentum capital rotated away on concerns about TPU share losses at Google. Mizuho notes optical and components names (where AVGO competes) are expected back in momentum favor later in 2026 as InP laser supply increases.

bullets.title: MU/ARM: Both at 52-week highs; MU +840% YTD, ARM +210% YTD; levered ETF rebalancing a key driver
bullets.body: Micron and ARM both hit 52-week highs; MU is up 840% YTD and ARM up 210% YTD. OPCO notes MU is up 209% since March 31 and AMD +164%, with SOXL needing $9B+ to rebalance on Monday — roughly one-third of typical monthly 401k equity flows — flagging that momentum may be ETF-driven rather than fundamentals-driven. Wolfe scheduled a semiconductor sector update call for June 22 covering AMD pre-quiet period and MU earnings.

bullets.title: CRM: Acquires Fin for $3.6B to expand Agentforce; Fin AI Agent at $100M+ ARR, +350% Y/Y
bullets.body: Salesforce acquired Fin for $3.6B to expand its Agentforce platform. Fin's AI agent is growing at $100M+ ARR with +350% year-over-year growth, positioning CRM to deepen its agentic AI footprint in enterprise customer service workflows.

bullets.title: MSFT: GitHub using AWS for incremental capacity despite planned full Azure migration by 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flagged that MSFT's GitHub is using AWS for incremental cloud capacity despite a plan to migrate fully to Azure by 2027 — a notable internal cloud defection that raises questions about the pace and completeness of Azure consolidation.

bullets.title: CRWV: +7.9% in Canadian trading on broad AI infrastructure strength
bullets.body: CoreWeave (CRWV) traded up 7.9% to C$21.80 in Canadian mid-morning trading, benefiting from the broader AI infrastructure/semiconductor momentum wave alongside WDC, STX, and memory names.

bullets.title: AAPL: Italian DMA probe on iOS cloud interoperability; Siri AI and foldable SKU in focus
bullets.body: Apple is facing a probe by Italy's antitrust regulator over DMA interoperability obligations, requiring iPhone maker to ensure third-party cloud providers can operate freely with iOS. Separately, Morgan Stanley's Tech Talk flagged AAPL Siri AI updates and a new foldable SKU as near-term catalysts to watch.

bullets.title: TLN/VST/OKLO: Power sector active; TLN closes $3.45B PJM acquisition, OKLO MOU on fuel recycling
bullets.body: Talen Energy completed its $3.45B acquisition of PJM natural gas assets from Energy Capital Partners, with IPPs TLN, VST, and NRG leading the utilities sector on Monday. OKLO entered an MOU with Standard Nuclear on nuclear fuel recycling and advanced fuel manufacturing. Goldman Sachs cited sustained AI data center power demand and geopolitical energy security concerns as long-term tailwinds for the sector.

bullets.title: BABA/Chinese ADRs: Under pressure as China AI price war intensifies; per-token costs down ~80% Y/Y
bullets.body: Chinese ADRs including BABA (-2.7% premarket) are under pressure as ByteDance, Tencent, Xiaomi, MiniMax, BABA, and DeepSeek slash model/API pricing 50-99%, with per-1M-token costs in China down ~80% Y/Y. DeepSeek separately raised $7.4B at a $50B+ valuation, becoming China's most valuable AI startup.

bullets.title: GOOGL: AI bidding expansion across Ads/PMax/Shopping; Gemini hits 27.7% ChatGPT share
bullets.body: Google is rolling out major AI-driven bidding updates (Smart Bidding Exploration) to Performance Max and Shopping campaigns, a potential positive for ad monetization. On the AI model side, Gemini reached 27.7% market share vs. OpenAI ChatGPT now below 50% for the first time, with Anthropic Claude at 10.3%.
